title: Finite presentation and smooth fibre dimensions in an algebraic devissage
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a finitely presented homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], let $N$ be a finitely presented $A$-module [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], and let $\mathfrak p\subset R$ be prime. Fix a complete algebra devissage $(A_i,B_i,M_i,\alpha_i)_{1\leq i\leq l}$ of $N/A/R$ over $\mathfrak p$ [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage]. All $A_i$ and $B_i$ are finitely presented $R$-algebras, all displayed ring maps are finitely presented, and $M_i$ is finitely presented both over $A_i$ and over $B_i$. Put $Q_i=\operatorname{coker}(\alpha_i)$, the quotient of $M_i$ by the image of $\alpha_i$. Then $Q_i$ is finitely presented over $B_i$. There exists $f\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ such that the localized data form a complete algebra devissage over $\mathfrak pR_f$ and, for each $i$, $Y_i=\operatorname{Spec}(B_i\otimes_R R_f)\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ is smooth, flat, and of finite presentation, with geometrically integral nonempty fibres of a constant dimension $a_i\geq0$. Here smoothness is [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], flatness is [def-weil-flat-morphism], geometrically integral means integral after every residue-field extension [def-pc-integral-scheme], and dimension is [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. For every scheme $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$, each fibre of $(Y_i)_T\to T$ is geometrically integral of dimension $a_i$; its unique generic point $\xi$ has $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(\xi)=a_i$, and every point of that fibre has transcendence degree at most $a_i$ [def-weil-residue-field], [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. No inequality between the different $a_i$ is asserted. Spectra and localization are [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and [def-weil-pbc-module-localization].

source.place: Tag 05HY (remark-finite-presentation), for finite presentation; smooth dimension preparation from morphisms.tex Tags 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), 02G2 (definition-smooth-relative-dimension), 01VF (lemma-smooth-flat), and varieties.tex Tag 0A21 (lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic), dimension of irreducible algebraic schemes over a field and transcendence degree of points.

proof.text: If $l=0$, there are no indexed conclusions, the given complete devissage has $N=0$, and $f=1$ suffices. Hence assume $l>0$. Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $g_i:\operatorname{Spec}B_i\to S$. By [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage] each $g_i$ is smooth. By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] it is flat and locally of finite presentation, and [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation], applied to the whole affine source and target, makes $R\to B_i$ finitely presented. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](2), $R\to A\to A_1$ and $R\to B_{i-1}\to A_i$ show that every $A_i$ is finitely presented over $R$.

source.place: Tags 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), 05HY (remark-finite-presentation); morphisms Tags 01VF and 01TQ; Algebra Tag 00F4(2)

proof.text: The maps $A\to A_1$ and $B_i\to A_{i+1}$ are already finitely presented by the devissage definition. For $B_i\to A_i$, the preceding step gives finite presentation of $A_i$ over $R$ and finite type of $B_i$ over $R$ (a finite presentation has finitely many generators). Thus [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-over-finite-type-algebra] gives finite presentation of $B_i\to A_i$. These, together with the structural maps just proved finitely presented, are all displayed ring maps.

source.place: Tag 00F4 (lemma-compose-finite-type), part (4), as used in flat.tex Tag 05HY

proof.text: Here is the elementary quotient calculation used in the induction. For a commutative ring $C$, a finitely presented module $P$ has a presentation $C^u\xrightarrow{D}C^v\to P\to0$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module]. For a map $\beta:C^r\to P$ with $r$ finite, lift its $r$ basis images to vectors $w_1,\ldots,w_r\in C^v$. Then $\operatorname{coker}\beta=C^v/(\operatorname{im}D+\sum_j Cw_j)$: both sides identify exactly the vectors whose images in $P$ belong to $\operatorname{im}\beta$. The matrix with columns those of $D$ and the $w_j$ is a finite presentation of this cokernel.

source.place: Tag 0519 (lemma-extension), part (4), finite-presentation quotient argument written out

proof.text: Induct on $i$ with inductive assertion that $M_i$ is finitely presented over $A_i$. Initially $N\cong M_1$ over $A$ and $A\to A_1$ is finite (it is surjective) and finitely presented; [lem-trf-finite-extension-module-finite-presentation] gives the assertion at $i=1$. At any stage $B_i\to A_i$ is finite by definition and finitely presented by step 2, so the same node gives finite presentation of $M_i$ over $B_i$. Apply step 3 with $C=B_i$, $P=M_i$, $\beta=\alpha_i$ to obtain finite presentation of $Q_i$. For $i<l$, $Q_i\cong M_{i+1}$ over $B_i$, and the surjective finitely presented map $B_i\to A_{i+1}$ is finite. The same finite-extension equivalence gives the inductive assertion for $i+1$. At the terminal index $Q_l=0$, consistent with the quotient calculation. This proves every module assertion without any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05HY (remark-finite-presentation), using Algebra Tag 0564 (lemma-finite-finitely-presented-extension) and Tag 0519

proof.text: By [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant] the function $d_i(x)=\dim_x((\operatorname{Spec}B_i)_{g_i(x)})$ is locally constant. Its values are nonnegative finite integers: the same cited statement identifies them with ranks of the finite locally free module of relative differentials. Every nonempty fibre is irreducible by [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. The restriction of $d_i$ to such a fibre is constant: two distinct values would partition the fibre into two disjoint nonempty open subsets (a level set and its complement), contradicting irreducibility [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The fibre over $\mathfrak p$ is nonempty; in the stated geometric-irreducibility convention this already follows from irreducibility, which includes nonemptiness. Let its constant value be $a_i$.

source.place: Tag 02G1 (lemma-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free), Tag 02G2 (definition-smooth-relative-dimension); elementary constancy on an irreducible fibre

proof.text: Set $E_i=\{x:d_i(x)=a_i\}$ and $U_i=g_i(E_i)$. The set $E_i$ is open by local constancy; $g_i$ is open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open], using flatness and local finite presentation from step 1. Thus $U_i$ is open and contains $\mathfrak p$. If $s\in U_i$, its fibre meets $E_i$, and constancy on that fibre shows the entire fibre belongs to $E_i$. Consequently $g_i^{-1}(U_i)=E_i$. The finite intersection $U=\bigcap_i U_i$ is an open neighbourhood of $\mathfrak p$. Write its closed complement as $V(I)$. Since $\mathfrak p\notin V(I)$, choose $f\in I\setminus\mathfrak p$; then $D(f)\subset U$. Thus all the restricted morphisms over $D(f)$ have nonempty fibres and local fibre dimension $a_i$ everywhere. The choice only compares points within each fibre and imposes no inequality between different indices.

source.place: Tag 056G (lemma-smooth-open), with Tags 02G1 and 02G2; Zariski principal neighbourhood selection written out

proof.text: Identify $\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ topologically with $D(f)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-spectrum-embedding]. The canonical tensor-localization identification is $B_i\otimes_RR_f\cong(B_i)_f$, $b\otimes(r/f^k)\mapsto rb/f^k$, with inverse $b/f^k\mapsto b\otimes f^{-k}$; the balanced relations check these maps are inverse. Its fibres over the corresponding primes are the original fibres: [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso] identifies the base residue fields, and the universal property of tensor products identifies both fibre rings with $B_i\otimes_R\kappa(s)$. By [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) the new morphisms are smooth. Their local fibre dimensions are $a_i$ by step 6, so they are smooth of relative dimension $a_i$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. They are flat and locally of finite presentation by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. The one-member affine cover of the target has affine inverse image, so [pqf-lem-affine-local-target] makes them affine morphisms; hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence](3), and therefore of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. The identification of each affine fibre with the spectrum of its tensor-product ring is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].

Check the complete devissage after localization. A finite algebra remains finite because the images of a finite module generating list generate its localization. Surjective ring maps remain surjective by lifting numerators; finite presentations remain finite by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1). Module isomorphisms localize to isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], localizing $B_i^{r_i}\to M_i\to Q_i\to0$ identifies the new cokernel with $(Q_i)_f$, hence with $(M_{i+1})_f$ for $i<l$, and with zero at the last index. Smoothness was checked in step 7; geometric irreducibility persists because its fibres are the old fibres over the same residue fields [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

For condition (7), let $\mathfrak p_i=\mathfrak pB_i$. Since the fibre over $\mathfrak p$ is nonempty, no $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ maps into $\mathfrak p_i$: otherwise its image in the fibre ring $B_i\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ would be both zero and a unit. In particular $f\notin\mathfrak p_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-prime-residue-field-iso], $(\mathfrak p_i)_f$ is prime and its residue field is canonically $\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$. Also $(\mathfrak pR_f)(B_i)_f=(\mathfrak p_i)_f$, directly by the generators of the extended ideals. Under this residue-field identification, the localized map $((B_i)_f)^{r_i}\to(M_i)_f$ tensored with the residue field is the original $\alpha_i\otimes\kappa(\mathfrak p_i)$: on a pure tensor $m/f^k\otimes c$ the identification sends it to $m\otimes f^{-k}c$. Thus it remains an isomorphism. Together with step 8 this verifies every condition of [def-trf-complete-algebra-devissage].

source.place: Tag 05HX (definition-complete-devissage-algebra), condition (7), and Algebra Tag 00E3, residue-field identification

proof.text: The nonempty fibres of each $Y_i\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ are geometrically irreducible, hence geometrically connected: an irreducible space is connected, since a disconnection would give two proper closed subsets covering it [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Apply [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] to this smooth morphism. It says that every field extension of every residue fibre is integral. In particular these fibres are geometrically integral, with precisely the quantifier over all residue-field extensions required in the item.

source.place: Tag 056T (lemma-smooth-geometrically-normal); geometric integrality of connected smooth fibres, as in more-morphisms.tex Tag 057J

proof.text: Let $T\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$ and $t\in T$, and let $s$ be its image. The fibre $F=((Y_i)_T)_t$ is $(Y_i)_s\times_{\kappa(s)}\kappa(t)$, by [lem-sc-fibre-dimension-after-base-change]. Step 10 makes $F$ integral and nonempty. By [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](1), applied to $Y_i$ and the map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to\operatorname{Spec}R_f$, $F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ is smooth of relative dimension $a_i$. Therefore [lem-sbc-smooth-fixed-dimension-over-field] gives $\dim F=a_i$. The same identification with a field extension, followed by any further extension of $\kappa(t)$, proves geometric integrality of $F$. No Noetherian or finite type hypothesis on $T$ was used.

The fibre $F$ is affine with coordinate ring $C=(B_i\otimes_R R_f)\otimes_{R_f}\kappa(t)$, a finitely presented, hence finite type, $\kappa(t)$-algebra by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-base-change-composition](1). As $F$ is integral, $C$ is a domain [def-pc-integral-scheme], so $(0)$ is its unique generic point $\xi$. Indeed the closure of the prime $\mathfrak q$ is $V(\mathfrak q)$; in a domain this equals the whole spectrum only for $\mathfrak q=0$. Apply [lem-sc-closed-irreducible-dimension-trdeg] first to $F$ itself to obtain $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(\xi)=\dim F=a_i$. For any $x\in F$, its closure $C_x=\overline{\{x\}}$ is a nonempty irreducible closed subset with generic point $x$, so the same node gives $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(x)=\dim C_x$. Every chain of irreducible closed subsets of $C_x$ is also such a chain in $F$, because $C_x$ is closed; hence $\dim C_x\leq\dim F=a_i$ directly from [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. This proves the last clause, including when $a_i=0$. The identification of each affine fibre with the spectrum of its tensor-product ring is [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra].
